songs.name: It's All Over Now Baby Blue

supporting_acts: New Riders of the Purple Sage

ai_show_review.summary: St. Stephen > Not Fade Away > Midnight Hour shines; soulful vocals throughout
ai_show_review.blurb: The set features a soaring St. Stephen > Not Fade Away > In The Midnight Hour suite and tight acoustic highlights such as Swing Low (Sweet Chariot). Jerry’s voice is clear and emotive, Pigpen adds a church‑y organ flavor, and the drummers drive crisp, energetic transitions. Overall the performance is tight, varied, and highly recommended.
ai_show_review.review: June 4 1970 at the Fillmore West captures the Dead in a period of both acoustic intimacy and electric firepower. The first set rolls through folk‑rock staples—Monkey And The Engineer, Deep Elem Blues, Friend Of The Devil—and builds to an inspired acoustic moment with Swing Low (Sweet Chariot) and Black Peter, where Jerry’s vocals are described as “sweet, lovely, and exceptionally clear.”  After a brief NRPS interlude the second set erupts: China Cat Sunflower seamlessly segues into I Know You Rider, then Attics Of My Life, before launching into a breathtaking St. Stephen > Not Fade Away > In The Midnight Hour sequence that many reviewers call “electrifying” and “drum‑driven.”  Pigpen’s organ adds a spooky, church‑y texture while Bob Weir’s guitar sits high in the mix with “superb noodling,” and both Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann provide crisp, tight drumming that propels the jams.  The Miller soundboard capture is praised for its excellent clarity—guitars front‑center, bright organ, and clean vocals—making it the definitive way to experience this legendary Fillmore night.

rating_calculation.sentiment_rationale: Four recordings describe the show in glowing terms (e.g., “excellent,” “stellar,” “electrifying”) while one is mixed; overall sentiment is strongly positive, warranting a high adjustment.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard source with crystal‑clear guitars, crisp drums and bright organ; captures the full show without gaps and highlights the standout St. Stephen > Not Fade Away > Midnight Hour sequence.

key_highlights: St. Stephen > Not Fade Away > In The Midnight Hour suite showcases tight, drum‑driven transitions
Acoustic gems Swing Low (Sweet Chariot) and Black Peter feature sweet, clear vocals
Pigpen’s organ adds a distinctive “churchy” texture throughout the set
Miller SBD delivers excellent clarity, making it the most complete listening experience
song_highlights: It's All Over Now Baby Blue

band_performance.Jerry: Vocals are sweet, clear and emotionally resonant—especially on Baby Blue and the acoustic numbers; he also adds tasteful pedal‑steel touches during the NRPS set.
band_performance.Bob: Guitar sits high in the mix with superb noodling; his lead work is tight and contributes heavily to the energy of the electric jams.
band_performance.Mickey: Drumming described as crisp, tight and ‘decidedly non‑country country,’ driving the transitions and adding power to the second set.
band_performance.Billy: Locks in tightly with Mickey, providing a solid rhythmic foundation that keeps the jam flow smooth.

must_listen_sequences: It's All Over Now Baby Blue
